column3: Close to the Hebrew; “a praise of David” is rendered “A Praise of David,” and “the king” is taken as address, “O King.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the majesty of the glory of your splendor” is rendered “the glorious splendor of Your majesty.”
Close to the Hebrew; “covenant loyalty” is rendered “mercy.”
Close to the Hebrew; “your godly ones” is rendered “Your saints.”
NKJV follows the Masoretic text, without the line about the LORD’s faithfulness found in the Septuagint and a Qumran scroll.
Close to the Hebrew; “wait” is rendered “look expectantly.”
Close to the Hebrew; וְחָסִיד (“loyal, kind”) is rendered “Gracious.”
